buildcraftfactory/item/water_gel: Draining an ocean is effective, but sometimes turning the surface into something solid is the more entertaining solution.
The Water Gelifier converts connected source water and aquatic plants into temporary Water Gel.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Check the Recipes and Usages sections together before crafting in bulk; this item may be an intermediate for several later machines.

Use the item while pointing at water. The first gel block is placed at the targeted water position and begins spreading through neighboring source water and supported aquatic plants. Water Gel advances through random ticks, so the randomTickSpeed gamerule directly affects how quickly it spreads and matures. While a non-spreading gel stage is still touching neighboring water it does not advance toward final solidification; once that surrounding water is gone, later random ticks can finish the process.

Only fully solidified Water Gel drops Gelled Water when broken. Earlier spreading or gelling stages do not provide the harvest item. The process is intended for controlled water removal and temporary construction, so test it on a small pool before applying it to an ocean.
buildcraftfactory/item/gel: It looks like water, feels rather less like water and no longer behaves like water at all.
Gelled Water is the solid material recovered from Water Gel.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Check the Recipes and Usages sections together before crafting in bulk; this item may be an intermediate for several later machines.
Use a Water Gelifier on source water and wait for the spreading gel to solidify. Breaking the completed gel yields Gelled Water.
buildcraftsilicon/block/laser: Some recipes require precision that a furnace, crafting grid and optimistic hammer cannot provide.
A Laser converts MJ into laser power for nearby compatible BuildCraft tables.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Several Lasers can work on one compatible table. Add them gradually and watch the table buffer so extra laser power is not built where it provides no benefit.

Place Lasers within six blocks of an Assembly, Charging, Integration, Advanced Crafting or Programming Table and supply the Lasers with MJ. Each Laser automatically searches for a compatible table that currently requests power.

A Laser can transfer up to 6.4 MJ per tick. Multiple Lasers may work on the same table, and their beams move as table demand changes.
buildcraftsilicon/block/assembly_table: Redstone and diamonds are useful ingredients, but some components require a much more precise arrangement of energy.
The Assembly Table uses laser power to manufacture BuildCraft components and pluggables.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Select only the recipes that should run automatically. Leaving unrelated recipes enabled can consume shared ingredients when several outputs are possible.

Insert the required ingredients and select one or more available assembly recipes. Nearby powered Lasers fill the selected recipe's energy requirement. When complete, the output is placed in the table or offered to adjacent inventories and pipes.

Several selected recipes may be cycled automatically when their ingredients are available. The table stores partial laser progress, so interrupted work can continue later.
buildcraftsilicon/block/charging_table: A portable machine without energy is merely a decorative machine that is inconvenient to carry.
The Charging Table uses MJ to charge Forge Energy items.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use filtered input and output inventories around the Charging Table so charged and uncharged items cannot circulate through the same loop indefinitely.

Place a chargeable item in the single slot. Supply MJ directly or with nearby Lasers; the table transfers whole energy units into items exposing the Forge Energy capability.

The table requests only the amount the item can still accept and stops when the item is full. Items that cannot receive energy are rejected.
buildcraftsilicon/block/integration_tabl: Some machines are built in one piece. Others become useful only after the important piece is installed.
The Integration Table installs compatible upgrades or components into a target item using laser power.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Prepare the exact gate, board or robot variant before insertion. Integration recipes often preserve or alter item data that is easier to verify before automation.

Place the target item in the center slot and the required components in the surrounding slots. If a registered integration recipe matches, nearby Lasers provide its required energy and the finished item appears in the output.

A major Robotics use is installing a programmed Redstone Board into an empty Robot. That operation requires 5,000 MJ.
buildcraftsilicon/block/advanced_craftin: Repeating the same crafting recipe is not difficult, but it is exactly the sort of work a machine should be doing instead.
The Advanced Crafting Table automatically repeats a configured crafting recipe using supplied materials and MJ.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep a buffer of each ingredient and extract completed results separately. Recirculating outputs into the ingredient side can block complex recipes.

Arrange the desired recipe in the phantom 3 by 3 blueprint grid, then supply matching ingredients to the material inventory. The table crafts the result into its output inventory whenever the recipe is valid and enough space is available. The Recipe Book can fill the phantom grid directly without consuming ingredients.

If several recipes match the same phantom grid, left-click the result preview for the next recipe or right-click for the previous one; the choice is saved.

Each operation requests 500 MJ. The table can receive MJ directly and also participates in the laser-table system.
buildcraftsilicon/block/programming_tabl: A blank board contains many possibilities and absolutely no useful instructions.
The Programming Table writes a selected robot career onto a blank Redstone Board using laser power.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Program commonly used boards in batches and label their storage. Career boards can look similar until installed in a robot.

Insert a blank Redstone Board, choose a career from the available options and power nearby Lasers. The table outputs a programmed board when the career's energy cost is reached.

Options are ordered by energy cost and name. Basic logistics careers cost 800 MJ; common work careers 3,200 MJ; advanced careers 12,800 MJ; and Builder costs 51,200 MJ.
buildcraftsilicon/item/redstone_crystal: Ordinary redstone dust is energetic, but a crystal is much easier to fit into precision machinery.
A Redstone Crystal is an Assembly Table component used by advanced BuildCraft recipes.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Check both recipes and usages before mass-producing this component. Silicon parts are often shared by several machines, gates and robot upgrades.
Produce Redstone Crystals in an Assembly Table with the ingredients shown by the recipe display. They are used in laser machinery, gates and other high-tier components.
buildcraftsilicon/item/gate_copier: A complicated Gate program is much easier to duplicate than to remember perfectly sixteen times.
The Gate Copier stores one Gate configuration and applies it to compatible Gates.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep one verified gate as the master and copy from it. This avoids propagating experimental settings through an entire pipe network.

Use the copier on a configured Gate to store its trigger, action, connection and parameter data. Use the filled copier on another compatible Gate to copy the stored program.

Sneak-right-click in the air to clear the stored data. The item model and tooltip indicate whether a program is currently stored.
buildcraftsilicon/item/plug_timer: A compact pipe network has little room for a tower of repeaters and clocks.
The Timer is a pipe pluggable that adds periodic 5, 10 and 15 second Gate triggers.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Configure the pluggable before copying or installing many of them. Test one pipe face first to confirm orientation and gate interaction.

Attach the Timer to a pipe. Gates on that pipe gain three internal triggers that pulse every 5, 10 or 15 seconds according to world game time.

The Timer occupies and blocks its side of the pipe like other pluggables.
buildcraftsilicon/item/chipset_red: Every good Gate starts with something more reliable than a pile of redstone dust.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Check both recipes and usages before mass-producing this component. Silicon parts are often shared by several machines, gates and robot upgrades.

buildcraftsilicon/item/chipset_quartz: Fine control is easier with a circuit built for precise conditions.

buildcraftsilicon/trigger/timer_long: Some jobs are worth waiting fifteen seconds between signals.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Connect the trigger to a temporary lamp first. Once its active and inactive states are confirmed, route the same signal to machinery.
The trigger becomes active on world ticks divisible by 300. Connect it to Gate actions that should repeat at a fixed interval.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/wood_power: A little MJ goes a long way once it leaves the engine.
The Wooden Kinesis Pipe extracts MJ from compatible adjacent energy sources and feeds it into a Kinesis Pipe network.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use one wooden extraction connection per intended source and avoid closed loops. Verify the source can safely provide the requested MJ rate.

Its default transfer limit is 16 MJ per tick. Wooden Kinesis Pipes do not connect directly to another wooden extraction pipe.

Power entering a junction is distributed proportionally among requesting outputs. A section accepts no more than its current free capacity, and the network preserves unaccepted energy instead of duplicating or discarding it during normal transfer.

Use Pipe Plugs or paint neighboring pipes different colors to prevent unwanted connections. Power-pipe limits are configured when the network changes and are restored after loading a world.

The guide uses per-tick rates. Live BuildCraft displays can show the equivalent per-second value when the Core time-gap setting is set to seconds.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/cobblestone_pow: Even the grandest factory needs somewhere to start.
The Cobblestone Kinesis Pipe is the basic low-capacity MJ transport pipe.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Choose pipe tiers by both throughput and network layout. A low-tier segment can limit an otherwise upgraded power line.

buildcraftenergy/item/oil: A dark liquid bubbling out of the ground is either a valuable energy resource or a very expensive environmental problem.
Oil is the naturally generated starting material for BuildCraft's fuel-processing chain.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep raw Oil in its own tank and leave room for intermediate products before starting an automated refinery.
Oil deposits generate in the world and can be collected with Buckets, a Pump or other compatible fluid handlers. Store it in Tanks and move it with Fluid Pipes.

Cool Oil is a dirty Combustion Engine fuel producing 3 MJ/t and Residue. Refining it is normally more valuable.

The Distiller uses the current temperature to choose a route: Cool Oil separates into Gaseous Fuel and Heavy Oil; Hot Oil separates into Mixed Light Fuel and Dense Oil; Searing Oil separates into Distilled Oil and Residue.
buildcraftenergy/item/oil_residue: Every elegant refining chain eventually produces something sticky that nobody wanted to store.
Residue is the heavy by-product of dirty fuels and several high-temperature distillation routes.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Residue is a real output, not waste to ignore. Provide a dedicated tank or controlled disposal route so refining cannot stop.

Crude Oil, Heavy Oil and Dense Oil produce Residue while burning in a Combustion Engine. It is also the liquid output of several Searing distillation recipes.

Residue is not registered as a Combustion Engine fuel. Drain it from engines and machines with Fluid Pipes or containers so residue tanks do not become blocked.

Like the other BuildCraft oil products, Residue has Cool, Hot and Searing states and can exchange heat in a Heat Exchanger. It is primarily a by-product and transportable process fluid in the current project.
buildcraftenergy/item/oil_heavy: The lighter fractions have left. What remains is still energetic, but considerably less cooperative.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Label Heavy Oil lines clearly and keep them separate from fuels; intermediate fluids may look similar in pipes and tanks.
Heavy Oil burns in a Combustion Engine at 2 MJ/t and produces Residue. It is usable directly, but further refining yields cleaner products.

Hot Heavy Oil distils into Light Fuel and Dense Oil. Searing Heavy Oil distils into Mixed Heavy Fuel and Residue. Use a Heat Exchanger to select the required temperature before sending it to the Distiller.
buildcraftenergy/item/oil_dense: Dense Oil contains the part of the original mixture that strongly objects to moving quickly through machinery.
Dense Oil is a dirty intermediate fuel obtained from Hot Oil or Hot Distilled Oil.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Store Dense Oil separately until the next processing step is ready. Feeding it into the wrong temperature stage wastes refinery capacity.
Dense Oil burns at 4 MJ/t in a Combustion Engine and produces Residue. Its higher output is useful when immediate power is more important than clean operation.
Heat Dense Oil to the Searing state and distil it to separate Dense Fuel from Residue. This is the final refining step for its branch of the processing chain.
buildcraftenergy/item/oil_distilled: The first pass removed the worst impurities. Several useful fractions are still sharing the same tank.

Cool Distilled Oil distils into Gaseous Fuel and Mixed Heavy Fuel. Hot Distilled Oil distils into Mixed Light Fuel and Dense Fuel. Change its temperature in a Heat Exchanger before choosing the next route.

Gaseous Fuel is the top output of distilling Cool Oil, Cool Distilled Oil or Cool Mixed Light Fuel. It has Cool, Hot and Searing forms for transport through the Heat Exchanger, although it does not require further distillation.

Use it when a machine needs the largest instantaneous output from one Combustion Engine. High output also adds heat quickly, so maintain a reliable coolant supply and an MJ consumer that can accept the generated power.
buildcraftenergy/item/fuel_light: Light Fuel is the sensible middle ground between a short energetic burst and a barrel that lasts all week.

Light Fuel combines high output with clean operation. Keep the engine cooled and ensure the connected MJ network can accept 6 MJ every tick.

The FE Engine consumes Forge Energy, converts it into MJ and behaves as a directional BuildCraft engine.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use the FE Engine when an FE network should power an MJ-only BuildCraft network without enabling automatic conversion for every ordinary machine.

The engine accepts FE into a 10,000 FE input buffer and produces 4 MJ/t by default. At the default 1 MJ = 10 FE ratio that consumes up to 40 FE/t. Generated MJ is held in the normal 1,000 MJ engine buffer and sent through the engine output face. The converter works even when Core power mode is MJ_ONLY.

The GUI has four upgrade slots and accepts one supported gear per slot. Each Iron Gear adds 2 MJ/t; each Gold Gear adds 3 MJ/t. The FE consumption rate follows the configured MJ/FE ratio, so changing power.mjPerFe changes the FE cost of the same MJ output.

Supply a redstone signal and rotate the engine so its moving end faces the MJ consumer or Kinesis Pipe. If the MJ buffer cannot accept another conversion pulse, the engine waits instead of consuming FE for power it cannot store. Like other non-Redstone engines it has heat and should not be left permanently blocked under load.

The four upgrade slots use the same rules as the FE Engine: each Iron Gear adds 2 MJ/t of conversion capacity and each Gold Gear adds 3 MJ/t. The actual FE/t result follows the configured MJ/FE ratio.

A redstone signal enables conversion. The Dynamo does not consume MJ for a pulse that would fill or overflow its FE buffer. When disabled, its stored FE slowly self-discharges by 1 FE per tick, matching the restored BuildCraft 8 converter behavior. Rotate it with a Wrench to choose the FE output face.
